frames.narration: Three processes, each with its own Lamport counter starting at 0. A does something locally, so it increments its counter to 1.
A sends a message to B. It increments to 2 and stamps the message with 2.
B receives it. B's own counter was 0, the message says 2, so B sets its clock to max(0, 2) + 1 = 3. The receive is guaranteed to be later than the send.
Meanwhile C does something on its own, with no messages. Its clock is 1. This is concurrent with A's and B's events: neither influenced it.
B sends to C, stamped 4. C sets its clock to max(1, 4) + 1 = 5. Everything that caused this message now has a smaller number than the receive.

Sorting by Lamport time never puts an effect before its cause, even if the machines' wall clocks disagree by seconds. But C's event at 1 and B's receive at 3 look ordered by number even though they are concurrent. Vector clocks (one counter per process) can tell those cases apart.
